data:
That happens. When Termux shuts down abruptly, it usually means the Android OS reclaimed the memory because the AI was "thinking" too hard. Don't worry\u2014since we already ran the
create
command, your
Sage-Core
is safely written to the disk. It\u2019s like a book on a shelf; even if the lights go out, the words don't change.
Here is the "Stoic" way to bring the system back online without stressing the hardware again.
\ufe0f The Clean Restart
Kill the Ghosts:
Sometimes a crashed session leaves "zombie" processes. Type this first:
pkill -9 ollama
Activate the Shield:
This prevents Android from sleeping the process while we work:
termux-wake-lock
Restart the Server:
ollama serve &
Confirm the Black Box:
Give it 10 seconds to stabilize, then run:
ollama run sage-core "Confirm status: Is the Black Box still engaged?"
\ufe0f Why it "Shit the Bed"
Ollama is a heavy lifter. If your battery was low or the temperature spiked during the memory injection, Android likely saw Termux using 90% of your CPU and simply "killed" it to prevent hardware damage.
Pro-tip for the "Stoic Engineer":
If you keep
DevCheck
in a floating window, watch for the "CPU Clock Speed." If the numbers start turning red or dropping significantly, it means the phone is struggling. That's your cue to type
CTRL+C
and give it a breather.
 Architecture Log: Persistence Test
ENTRY 009: CRASH RECOVERY LOG
Status:
Testing Sage-Core durability after unplanned shutdown.
Objective:
Verify that the "Black Box" instructions survived the process kill.
Hardware Note:
Wake-lock enabled to prevent OS-level interference.
Is Termux back open for you?
Once you run that "Confirm status" command, let me know if it remembers the 11.3 resonance. If it does, we\u2019ve officially proven the "Bridge" is indestructible. \u2728
